question: Build a balance-sheet comp table for four U.S. retailers: TJX Companies, Ross Stores, Lowe's and Tractor Supply. Use each company's latest reported balance sheet as of October 3, 2026 (the most recent 10-Q or 10-K) and state its balance-sheet date. Report, in USD millions: (1) cash and cash equivalents (exclude short-term investments and restricted cash); (2) total debt = current portion of long-term debt + long-term debt (non-current portion), as presented on the face of the balance sheet, excluding operating lease liabilities, separately presented finance lease liabilities and any commercial paper or short-term borrowings; (3) net debt = total debt - cash and cash equivalents (a negative number means net cash).
grading: Graded cell by cell: each value within tolerance and for the stated period; a missing cell counts as wrong.

output.answer:
## Important note on the "October 3, 2026" reference

None of these four companies has a balance-sheet date of October 3, 2026, and none had filed a report covering that date as of early October 2026. Fiscal Q3 for these retailers ends later in the quarter (Ross/TJX: Oct 31, 2026; Lowe's: Oct 30, 2026; Tractor Supply: Sept 26, 2026 — with its Q3 10-Q not due until its Oct 22, 2026 earnings date). So below is the **latest reported balance sheet available as of October 3, 2026**, with each actual balance-sheet date stated, per your instruction.

## Balance-sheet comp table (USD millions, as presented on the face of the balance sheet)

| Company | Balance-sheet date | Filing | (1) Cash & cash equivalents | Current portion of LTD | Long-term debt (non-current) | (2) Total debt | (3) Net debt |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TJX Companies | Aug 1, 2026 | 10-Q (Q2 FY2027) | 6,004 | 1,000 | 1,871 | **2,871** | **(3,133)** |
| Ross Stores | Aug 1, 2026 | 10-Q (Q2 FY2026) | 4,288 | 241 | 777 | **1,018** | **(3,270)** |
| Lowe's | Jul 31, 2026 | 10-Q (Q2 FY2026) | 3,172 | 2,352 | 35,204 | **37,556** | **34,384** |
| Tractor Supply | Jun 27, 2026 | 10-Q (Q2 FY2026) | 232 | 0 | 2,154 | **2,154** | **1,922** |

Negative net debt = net cash. TJX and Ross are both in a net-cash position; Lowe's and Tractor Supply are net-debt.

## Sourcing and line-item notes

**TJX Companies** — Cash and cash equivalents $6,004M; current portion of long-term debt $1,000M; long-term debt $1,871M. No short-term bank borrowings or commercial paper outstanding as of Aug 1, 2026. Current portion of operating lease liabilities ($1,714M) excluded; no separately presented finance lease liabilities.
Source: [TJX 10-Q, quarter ended Aug 1, 2026 (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/109198/000010919826000048/tjx-20260801.htm)

**Ross Stores** — Cash and cash equivalents $4,288,124K; current portion of long-term debt $241,459K; long-term debt (due beyond one year) $777,053K. Restricted cash and cash equivalents ($68,800K, split between prepaid expenses and other long-term assets) excluded per your instruction. Operating lease liabilities excluded; no separate finance lease liabilities presented. Ross reports no separate short-term investment line — its securities holdings sit inside cash and cash equivalents.
Source: [Ross Stores 10-Q, quarter ended Aug 1, 2026 (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/745732/000074573226000041/rost-20260801.htm)

**Lowe's** — Cash and cash equivalents $3,172M (short-term investments of $235M and long-term investments excluded); current maturities of long-term debt $2,352M; long-term debt, excluding current maturities $35,204M. No short-term borrowings/commercial paper line on the Q2 face (Q1 had carried $380M of commercial paper, since repaid). A nuance: Lowe's does not present finance lease liabilities separately on the balance sheet — they are embedded in the "Long-term debt, excluding current maturities" line (its fair-value note discloses unsecured notes "excluding finance lease obligations and the 2025 Term Loan"; the $5.0B notes issued in late 2025 are included).
Source: [Lowe's 10-Q, quarter ended Jul 31, 2026 (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/60667/000006066726000117/low-20260731.htm) and [Q2 2026 results release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lowes-reports-second-quarter-2026-sales-and-earnings-results-302854643.html)

**Tractor Supply** — Cash and cash equivalents $231,588K ($232M); no current portion of long-term debt (the debt note shows the current portion as zero); long-term debt $2,153,826K. Finance lease liabilities (current $10,315K; non-current $42,933K) and operating lease liabilities (current $463,556K; non-current $3,874,348K) are separately presented and therefore excluded, as are letters of credit ($38.6M).
Source: [Tractor Supply 10-Q, quarter ended Jun 27, 2026 (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/916365/000091636526000059/tsco-20260627.htm) and [Q2 2026 results release](https://corporate.tractorsupply.com/newsroom/news-releases/news-releases-details/2026/Tractor-Supply-Company-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-Updates-Fiscal-Year-2026-Outlook/default.aspx)

**Methodology:** Total debt = current portion of long-term debt + non-current long-term debt, exactly as those lines appear on each balance-sheet face. Excluded: operating lease liabilities, separately presented finance lease liabilities, and short-term borrowings/commercial paper (none outstanding for any of the four at these dates). Net debt = total debt − cash and cash equivalents (restricted cash and short-term/long-term investments excluded).
